title: Rabbi Chanan, Father of Rabbi Shimon
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.5.6): “Rabbi Yoni said: I went to the South and heard Rabbi Chanan, the father of Rabbi Shimon, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.” In [Chullin 132b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.132b.6) it reads simply “the elders of the South.” Hyman also reports the statement in the Jerusalem Talmud on Chullin then newly printed, folio 73a. The scholar R. Z. Babar (באבאר) wrote in HaKedem, part 1, p. 33, that this Amora is not found anywhere. Hyman objects that he did not see the above Jerusalem Talmud on Peah. His son Rabbi Shimon is mentioned in Midrash Tehillim 78:17.[^2]

notes.text: The supplied באבאר is retained as Babar rather than silently identified as Bacher. Hyman reports the then newly printed “Jerusalem Talmud on Chullin”; this is an attributed historical bibliographical claim, not an assertion that the work is canonical or newly published now. His criticism of the scholar remains his own.

The linked Peah has Rabbi Yose describe hearing Rabbi Chanan, father of Rabbi Shimon, and has Shimon parenthesized in “Rabbi (Shimon) ben Levi.” [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1420&lang=en) abbreviates the teacher as רשב״ל. Hyman writes Rabbi Yoni and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. The linked Bavli attributes the parallel ruling to the elders of the South.
